## Data Model Signals

### Entities Revealed
- **Stage** — a named classification assigned to a contact (Person)
  - `id` (numeric or UUID)
  - `name` (string) — e.g., "Seller Prospect", "Lead"
  - `people_count` (integer) — count of Person records currently assigned to this stage
  - `sort_order` (integer) — controls display order, reorderable via drag
  - `is_system` (boolean) — true for Lead, Closed, Trash (protected, non-editable/deleteable)
  - `account_id` (FK to the FUB account/brokerage)

- **Person** — has a `stage_id` foreign key linking to Stage

### Enum Values (stage names observed)
The following stage names are in use for this account:
1. `Seller Prospect`
2. `Lead` (system)
3. `A - Hot 1-3 Months`
4. `B - Warm 3-6 Months`
5. `C - Cold 6+ Months`
6. `Renter - future buyer`

14. `Real Estate Agent`
15. `Vendor`
16. `Nurture`

### Relationships
- Stage → People: one-to-many (one Stage has many People)
- Stage → Account: many-to-one (stages are account-scoped)
- People count is a derived aggregate, not a stored field

### Pagination model
No pagination — stages list appears to be loaded in full. With 16 entries, this is small enough for a single page load.

### Notable data patterns
- The naming convention `A - Hot 1-3 Months`, `B - Warm 3-6 Months`, `C - Cold 6+ Months` suggests a temperature-based lead classification system with a time-horizon component
- "Trash" has 47 contacts despite being a system stage — contacts can be moved to Trash but it's read-only in terms of configuration
- "Real Estate Agent" (2,342 people) is the third largest stage — indicating the account tracks agent-sphere contacts distinctly from buyer/seller leads
- "Seller Prospect" (7,523) vs "Lead" (8,243) suggests roughly half the contact base skews toward seller prospects

## Rebuild Notes

### Component Breakdown

```
<AdminLayout>
  <GlobalTopNav activeItem="admin" />
  <AdminSubNav activeTab="stages" />
  <PageContent>
    <StagesPage>
      <StagesCard>
        <CardHeader>
          <h2>Stages</h2>
          <AddStageButton onClick={openAddStageModal} />
        </CardHeader>
        <StagesTable>
          <TableHeader>
            <ColHeader>Stage Name</ColHeader>
            <ColHeader align="right">People</ColHeader>
            <ColHeader align="right">Actions</ColHeader>
          </TableHeader>
          <DraggableList onReorder={handleReorder}>
            {stages.map(stage => (
              <StageRow
                key={stage.id}
                stage={stage}
                onEdit={openEditStageModal}
                onDelete={openDeleteConfirm}
              />
            ))}
          </DraggableList>
        </StagesTable>
      </StagesCard>
    </StagesPage>
  </PageContent>
  <GettingStartedBar />
  <HelpButton />
</AdminLayout>
```

### `<StageRow>` sub-structure
```
<StageRow>
  <DragHandle />                        {/* 6-dot grid icon, always visible */}
  <StageName>{stage.name}</StageName>   {/* plain text, 14px */}
  <PeopleCount>
    {stage.people_count > 0
      ? <Link href={`/people?stage=${stage.id}`}>{stage.people_count.toLocaleString()}</Link>
      : <span>0</span>
    }
  </PeopleCount>
  <Actions>
    {!stage.is_system && (
      <>
        <EditIcon onClick={() => onEdit(stage)} />
        <DeleteIcon onClick={() => onDelete(stage)} />
      </>
    )}
  </Actions>
</StageRow>
```

### Key implementation notes

1. **Drag-to-reorder:** Use a library like `react-beautiful-dnd` or `@dnd-kit/core`. On drop, PATCH/PUT the updated `sort_order` for all affected stages via API. Optimistic UI update the list immediately.

2. **System stages protection:** The `is_system` flag (or equivalent) on Lead, Closed, and Trash stages suppresses the edit/delete action icons entirely — these rows render no `<Actions>` column content.

3. **People count as link vs plain text:** Conditional rendering — if `people_count > 0`, render as `<a>` with blue styling; if 0, render as gray `<span>`. The link URL likely maps to the People list view with a stage filter applied.

4. **People count format:** Numbers with 4+ digits use comma separators (7,523; 8,243; 2,342). Zero is displayed as "0" (not "—" or empty).

5. **"Add Stage" modal [INFERRED]:** Likely a simple modal with:
   - A text input labeled "Stage Name" (required)
   - Save / Cancel buttons
   - On save, appends the new stage to the end of the list with `people_count: 0`

6. **"How Stages work" help link:** Renders as a secondary text-link button with an info icon prefix, positioned at the far right of the sub-nav bar (floated right or flex justify-between on the sub-nav row).

7. **Sub-nav overflow:** The "More ▾" tab with a caret indicates there are additional admin sub-sections not visible in the horizontal tab strip at default viewport width. Clicking reveals a dropdown of overflow items.

8. **Table has no outer border** — the card's box-shadow provides visual separation, not a table border. Row dividers are thin 1px `border-bottom` on each row except the last.

9. **Drag handle always visible** (not hover-only) based on the screenshot — all rows show the 6-dot handle regardless of hover state.

10. **Stage ordering significance:** The order of stages in this list determines the order they appear in dropdowns when agents assign stages to contacts throughout the FUB UI (contact record, lead routing, action plans, etc.).

11. **Account scoping:** The `/2/` in the URL (`ryan-realty.followupboss.com/2/stages`) indicates account ID `2` — stages are scoped per account, not global to FUB.

12. **No inline edit:** Based on the presence of a dedicated edit icon, stage editing likely happens via a modal, not inline row editing.
